receipts.first_text_witness: You know that feeling when you're grinding at work, constantly thinking about money, but you're absolutely exhausted, your relationships are suffering, you're checking your portfolio obsessively every single day, and if you stop for even a second, you feel like everything falls apart. Sound familiar?
receipts.last_text_witness: which means letting your money do the work while you live your actual life. That's real wealth, and that's worth far more than a fancy car or expensive house or whatever else society tells you that you're supposed to want. Build your systems, automate your wealth building, then just focus on living. Your future self will thank you for having the discipline to do this the right way, the rights.

primary_source_receipts.locator: Vanguard April 2025 emergency-savings research (12,443 investors, CFPB Financial Well-Being Scale) via CNBC/Motley Fool coverage
primary_source_receipts.finding: Investors with $2,000+ in emergency savings scored 21% higher on financial well-being than those with none, after controls; 3-6 months of expenses associated with a 13% increase; time on finances 7.3 vs 3.7 hours/week.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Vanguard paper not read directly; correlational survey of Vanguard investors, not representative.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 79% of active large-cap U.S. equity funds underperformed the S&P 500 in 2025 (65% in 2024); 55% mid-cap and 41% small-cap underperformed their benchmarks.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Scorecard not read directly; long-horizon category counts not confirmed in the summary.
